title: Six lessons learned from NFL Week 9: Arvell Reese a superstar in the making, C.J. Stroud having career year - CBS Sports
description: Plus, there's a bell cow running back emerging for one of the NFL's best teams
body:
Plus, there's a bell cow running back emerging for one of the NFL's best teams
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the trade deadline today, I am reminded that self-awareness is of one of the best attributes an organization can have, from top to bottom.The team that comes to mind immediately is one we've heard a lot from -- not in a good way -- this year: the Colts. Around this time last year, Indianapolis sent away two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner in a trade-deadline blockbuster. Indianapolis was 7-2 at the time, but was it really a team that needed to go all-in? No. Daniel Jones was playing so over-his-head well, and a smart front office would have recognized the great record was a product of a very soft schedule, a little bit of luck and an unprecedented hot streak. There was no rush here. The 2025 season was supposed to be a transition one, and a medium-sized cornerback addition would have been fine. Again, just a few months earlier, Indianapolis was basically taking a flyer on Jones.You know how the rest of the story goes. Jones and the offense start to fall off, then Jones ruptures his Achilles. Now, the Colts are 2-7 and in the midst of a franchise-altering sale while not even owning their first-round pick. If the draft started today, Indianapolis would send the No. 4 pick to the Jets. Yikes!The Jets, meanwhile, continue to profit in a big way off of that trade and the Quinnen Williams trade. They currently own the No. 4 (Colts'), No. 6 (their own) and No. 13 (Cowboys') picks. They knew this would be a long process. They knew it could be ugly for a while, and this year's 2-7 mark confirms that. But New York could have a terrific kickstart to their rebuild in a few months' time.
One team fell for fool's gold. The other knew exactly where it was and embraced its unenviable role.The Jets are still waiting to fully invest in their rebuild. The other New York team? Well, it has already started -- and is way ahead of schedule -- thanks to a different type of self-awareness.1. Arvell Reese is a superstar in the makingPlease just watch these highlights first, then pick your jaw up from off the floor and continue reading below.
Some fun stats for you:Reese is the youngest player with a three-sack game since the stat became official for individuals in 1982 Reese is the only player in the NFL with 65 tackles, eight tackles for loss and an interception this season.Reese is the first rookie to hit all three of those milestones within his team's first eight games since Luke Kuechly in 2012.The biggest question surrounding Reese during the build-up to the NFL Draft was "Where do you play him?"The answer should have been another question: "Why does it matter?"And the Giants were exactly right to take that approach. Reese was an EDGE at Ohio State who moonlighted at off-ball linebacker. When the Giants initially drafted him, John Harbaugh basically said he'd play linebacker but also move around. Through eight games, Reese has now played at least 30 snaps at seven different spots: right inside linebacker, left inside linebacker, right linebacker, right EDGE, left linebacker, middle linebacker and left EDGE.This is the way the NFL is trending. Think about guys such as Seattle's Nick Emmanwori, technically a safety who really plays everywhere, and someone we've talked about in this column before. Reese is of that ilk: a truly, laughably absurd athlete. A weapon who transcends positional labels. His strip sack of Joe Milton happened in 2.29 seconds, the fastest sack of the year per Next Gen Stats.
Here's where the self-awareness portion comes in. The Giants knew neither they nor Reese had to have it figured out on Day 1. The Giants are in Year 1 under John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Reese is 21 years old. The world was (and still is!) their oyster to experiment. Reese looks phenomenal. The Giants are 5-2-1 despite having started three different quarterbacks, and players such as Reese give them a bright future, too.2. C.J. Stroud is the best quarterback you're not paying attention toI do not blame you if you didn't watch -- or even think twice (or once) -- about the Texans-Chargers Week 9 matchup. The Chargers are unwatchable, and the Texans are middling after coming into the season with Super Bowl expectations.What you missed and may have missed for much of this season, though, is C.J. Stroud playing outstanding football. He threw five touchdown passes Sunday, and his highlights ranged from heart-warming ...
(Welcome back, Tank Dell!)... to jaw-dropping.
Lest you think "Oh, it's just the Chargers," they've actually been decent on defense this year. This was just Stroud putting on a clinic. It's been this way all year.C.J. Stroud this yearNFL rankCareer-best?TD-Int16-22ndYesPassing success rate48.7%11thYesNegative play rate6.9%6thYesEPA per dropback0.186thYesThe Texans' 3-5 record is mostly due to a surprisingly up-and-down defense and major struggles on the ground. DeMeco Ryans hasn't been great situationally, either. Even if Houston doesn't make the playoffs, Stroud's play is huge for Stroud himself -- he entered the year without an extension on his rookie deal -- and for Houston, which can feel much better about handing Stroud said extension.On a week in which Jordan Love and Joe Burrow stole the spotlight, don't forget about Stroud.3. The Vikings need to trade for a quarterbackDid you watch Monday night?I could leave it there, but I won't. Carson Wentz isn't the answer -- clearly. Kyler Murray has never looked comfortable in this offense. Is Geno Smith the answer? A reunion with Kirk Cousins? It can't be worse than it's been, and Minnesota simply cannot waste this defense again.4. Jonah Coleman taking over the Broncos' backfield is a good thing for DenverJonah Coleman recorded 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers. He played 53 of Denver's 65 snaps, second-most of any skill-position player behind Courtland Sutton. He also played nine of Denver's 10 third-down snaps.J.K. Dobbins, on the other hand, played just nine snaps overall, and zero on third down. After some injuries earlier this year, Coleman owns this backfield -- especially until RJ Harvey returns -- and that's a good thing.Broncos RBs this seasonColemanDobbinsHarveyYards per rush4.13.63.3Explosive run rate9%5%0%Yards per rush vs. 8-man box5.41.61.0Pct of runs with missed tackle forced17%14%4%Coleman already has as many rushing touchdowns (three) as Dobbins has despite having less than half of Dobbins' carries.
Let's remember that Coleman is a fourth-round rookie, too. He should continue to get better. Denver's reportedly been shopping around for running backs, but if it doesn't land one, Coleman will emerge as an early-down bell cow (with Harvey more in the mix on late downs) down the stretch.Just, please, Sean Payton, no more pitch plays in late-game, wind-the-clock scenarios. I think Bo Nix agrees.5. Evan Williams is a starWe highlighted Evan Williams a few weeks ago, but that was really more about Jonathan Gannon. After a game that included an incredible interception, four pressures and five tackles, Williams gets his own slot here.The four pressures were a season high for Williams, who blitzed a season-high eight times. On one blitz, he basically shoulder-checked Rhamondre Stevenson (a good pass-blocking back) to the side and forced a throwaway. On another, he didn't get near Drake Maye but tracked back and limited Maye's scramble to 3 yards. On his final blitz of the day, he ran right by Lan Larison and nearly got a strip sack.Williams is a combination of a high-speed train and a bumper car attacking the quarterback. If you don't try to stop him, he'll chase you down, and when you do try to stop him, he bounces off and keeps going. He now has a ridiculous 38.2% pressure rate on 34 pass-rush snaps this season.Oh yeah, and did we mention he can do this on the back end?
And this?
Now for the numbers:Williams is PFF's No. 1-graded safety this year: first in coverage and sixth in rush defense.He makes a tackle on 15.5% of his snaps against the run, the fifth-highest rate among 84 defensive backs with at least 400 snaps entering "Monday Night Football."Individual coverage tracking can be iffy, but Williams is allowing 3.8 yards per attempt as the primary defender, 10th out of 195 players who had been targeted at least 20 times entering "Monday Night Football."His passer rating allowed -- 36.2 -- is even better: fourth out that same 195-player sample. For reference, throwing the ball incomplete every play would result in a 39.6 passer rating.Good player. Really, really good player. All-Pro player.6. The NFC South is approaching all-time bad territoryIt was a rough week for the NFC South. The Falcons got shellacked by the Bengals in Madrid, the Panthers lost at home to the Broncos, and the Buccaneers wasted five Bears turnovers in a loss in Chicago. The division's lone winner -- the Saints -- got an uninspiring 23-22 overtime win over Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. A failed two-point conversion is all that stood between the NFC South and an 0-4 week.The 2026 NFC South is the only division ever with every team at least two games below .500 through Week 9. The Panthers and the Saints are 3-5, and the Buccaneers and the Falcons are 3-6. The combined 12-22 record is on pace to be the third-worst by any division since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.SportsLine currently does not project any NFC South team to reach eight wins. There's never been a seven-win playoff team in the 17-game era (since 2021).But SportsLine projections also has every team reaching at least six wins, setting up for some major late-season drama. Remember last year, when the Buccaneers beat the Panthers to take the NFC South lead in Week 18, only for Carolina to win the division thanks to a tiebreaker because the Falcons beat the Saints the next day? Yeah, prepare for some weirdness.

title: Can Carson Beck convince the Cardinals not to draft a QB? He has eight games to make his case - CBS Sports
description: The third-round rookie has eight games to prove he can be this year's Tyler Shough, but history says that won't b
body:
The third-round rookie has eight games to prove he can be this year's Tyler Shough, but history says that won't be easy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Carson Beck wasn't supposed to be the Cardinals' starting quarterback in 2026. But after Jacoby Brissett was benched-and-then-traded to Baltimore following Week 8's loss, and then, seven days later, Gardner Minshew suffered an elbow injury that could require season-ending surgery, those best-laid plans have suddenly changed.Now the third-round rookie is in line to make his NFL debut against the Rams this Sunday. And Beck will have eight games to convince the Cardinals they don't need to use what will almost certainly be a top-10 pick on another quarterback next spring.(I say "almost certainly" because while the Cards are currently 3-6 and everything appears to be going wrong, a year ago at this time, the Saints were 1-7, turned to Tyler Shough to finish 5-4 and ended up with the eighth pick instead of something higher. Shorter version: We'll see.) That's a potentially franchise-changing opportunity for the 65th overall pick, but what exactly would success look like?
Back in June, I wrote that Beck might be the safest quarterback in the 2026 draft class. The former Georgia and Miami QB had started 43 games, was a quick processor, took care of the football and kept the offense on schedule. His 38.6% first-down rate ranked in the 95th percentile among draft-eligible quarterbacks from 2015-26.But there was a catch. Beck faced pressure on just 19.1% of his college dropbacks, the lowest rate among quarterbacks going back more than a decade, and more than 32% of his throws were screens. He was rarely asked to make something happen when everything around him fell apart because it so rarely did.That was a big question entering the NFL: Was Beck's high floor the product of his talent, his surroundings or some combination of both? Well, we're about to find out.
What history tells us about late-season rookie auditionsSince 2007, 24 quarterbacks drafted in the third round or later made their first NFL start after Week 7 of their rookie seasons. (This is through the 2024 draft class so we can look at Year 2 production, as well.)Of those 24, only eight started at least four games as rookies. And just three of those eight – Nick Foles, Desmond Ridder and Brock Purdy – started at least eight games the following season. Sam Howell was the only quarterback with fewer than four rookie starts to do so.How late-starting rookie QBs drafted in Round 3 or later fared in Year 2QuarterbackRoundRookie startsYear 2 startsNick Foles (2012)3610Desmond Ridder (2022)3412John Skelton (2010)547T.J. Yates (2011)540Keith Null (2009)640Ryan Lindley (2012)640Zach Mettenberger (2014)663Brock Purdy (2022)7516What's interesting is that six of those eight quarterbacks improved their yards per attempt between their first two and final two rookie starts. But that improvement didn't necessarily translate to long-term success.Ridder, for example, went from 5.3 yards per attempt in his first two starts to 7.0 in his final two, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Atlanta handed Ridder the starting job in 2023 but benched him twice that season before trading him to Arizona the following March. The Falcons then drafted Michael Penix Jr. eighth overall in 2024.Purdy, obviously, was very different. He averaged 8.6 yards per attempt with four touchdowns and no interceptions in his first two starts, then maintained that production over his final two. He didn't need to improve dramatically because he'd already shown he could play. Now he's one of the league's best quarterbacks.Passing on a QB isn't the same as finding oneFive of those eight teams didn't draft a quarterback the following spring. But several drafted one within the next year or two, and where they picked tells us plenty about the decisions they made.Rookie QBNext draft: first pick usedNext QB draftedFoles2013: No. 4, Lane JohnsonMatt Barkley, 2013 (R4, No. 98)Ridder2023: No. 8, Bijan RobinsonMichael Penix Jr., 2024 (R1, No. 8)Skelton2011: No. 5, Patrick PetersonRyan Lindley, 2012 (R6, No. 185)Yates2012: No. 26, Whitney MercilusTom Savage, 2014 (R4, No. 135)Null2010: No. 1, Sam BradfordSam Bradford, 2010 (R1, No. 1)Lindley2013: No. 7, Jonathan CooperLogan Thomas, 2014 (R4, No. 120)Mettenberger2015: No. 2, Marcus MariotaMarcus Mariota, 2015 (R1, No. 2)Purdy2023: No. 87, Ji'Ayir BrownKurtis Rourke, 2025 (R7, No. 227)The Cardinals know this story better than most. Injuries forced them to start rookies John Skelton in 2010 and Ryan Lindley in 2012, but neither was viewed as the long-term answer. Arizona took Patrick Peterson fifth overall in 2011, passing on quarterbacks Jake Locker, Blaine Gabbert and Andy Dalton, then selected Jonathan Cooper seventh overall in 2013, ahead of Geno Smith. Instead of drafting a quarterback, the Cardinals traded for veterans Kevin Kolb and Carson Palmer in those respective offseasons.That's why draft position matters. Tennessee had the No. 2 overall pick in 2015 and used it on Marcus Mariota after Zach Mettenberger's six rookie starts. St. Louis took Sam Bradford first overall in 2010, but Keith Null had only started four games because injuries forced the Rams to turn to their sixth-round rookie.San Francisco's situation was different. The 49ers traded up to draft Trey Lance third overall in 2021, but he suffered a season-ending ankle injury in Week 2 of '22. Jimmy Garoppolo took over, then broke his foot in Week 13, giving Purdy, the final pick of the 2022 draft, his opportunity. Purdy won all five of his regular-season starts, then two playoff games, and by the following season he'd taken the job Lance was drafted to fill.Could Tyler Shough be Beck's blueprint?If there's a recent example Beck should hope to follow, it's Tyler Shough. The Saints selected him 40th overall in 2025, and he took over the starting job in Week 9, giving New Orleans nine games to evaluate him.Shough went 5-4, but it was how he played that mattered. He completed nearly 68% of his passes, made smart decisions and showed he could run the offense without the Saints having to protect him. It wasn't always pretty, but it was enough for New Orleans to pass on drafting another QB in 2026 and enter the season believing Shough could be its long-term answer.That's the goal for Beck. He doesn't need to become a superstar overnight, but he does need to give Mike LaFleur enough confidence to build around him instead of looking for his replacement – which is exactly what the Saints did in April when they used the No. 8 pick on wide receiver Jordyn Tyson.And there's reason to think this offense should suit him. Arizona has attempted 58.8% of its passes within five yards of the line of scrimmage, while the offensive line has allowed pressure on 31.1% of dropbacks – the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL, according to TruMedia. Beck's accuracy, anticipation and ability to play on time should, in theory, translate. (The game, I need to remind myself, is not a theoretical exercise, so … we'll see.)But Arizona also ranks 28th in yards per play, and Brissett and Minshew had not consistently turned those manageable throws into meaningful production. Beck's challenge is to turn those short throws into more first downs and points.In my preseason projections for the 2026 rookie quarterbacks, I had Beck averaging 6.9 yards per attempt with an 85.8 passer rating – solid numbers that would be an improvement over Arizona's quarterback play to date. But just as important will be whether Beck gets better over the next two months.The Cardinals don't need to reel off eight straight wins, but they do need to see how Beck responds when defenses take away the easy throws. Can he push the ball downfield, keep drives alive under pressure and avoid costly mistakes?At Miami last season, Beck showed that he can be an efficient game manager – and his preseason debut suggested those skills could translate. Now comes the part that actually matters: proving he can do it against NFL starters, week after week, when opponents know exactly what he wants to do.And with a possible top-10 pick awaiting Arizona in April, there's a lot at stake – for the rookie quarterback and an organization that last had a winning season in 2021 (and before that, 2015). Beck doesn't have to prove he's a franchise quarterback during his two-month audition, but he does have to give the Cardinals a reason to believe he could become one.

        Trinidad Chambliss was untouchable at home and downright impressive whenever he faced Georgia last season.But not on Saturday. The Ole Miss quarterback, who accounted for five touchdowns in two games against the Bulldogs last season, was drilled 42-7 at home by Georgia in a lopsided loss that likely ended the Rebels' playoff dreams. Georgia was magnificent in the road win Saturday, sacking Chambliss four times and holding him without a touchdown throw for the first time in 22 games while also snapping Ole Miss' 16-game home winning streak.The impressive performance (and Miami's loss at Notre Dame) lifts Georgia to No. 1 in the Week 11 CBS Sports College Football Power Rankings."I feel like we could have put up 60," said Georgia safety KJ Bolden, who returned an interception 26 yards. "We got a little relaxed. We could have pitched a shutout. I don't have regular standards like everybody else. Our standards are pretty high here."
This was nothing new for Georgia. The Bulldogs seemed invincible until the inexplicable loss to Auburn at home, but they're back after back-to-back dominating performances against Florida and Ole Miss. Falling 10 spots after a dismal home outing, Ole Miss is this week's biggest mover. Tennessee and Wake Forest are our biggest risers.Don't worry, Notre Dame fans, you're getting some love, too. The Irish climb to No. 2 after an impressive 31-24 win over former No. 1 Miami, which struggled in the first half as quarterback Darian Mensah adjusted to life without superstar receiver Malachi Toney before rallying twice to make it a single-score game in the second half.
Two unbeatens remain -- Utah and UCLA -- but would you believe neither is inside the top five? The strength of competition just isn't quite up to top-5 consideration.

We're handing out grades for every team that played in Week 9

        Welcome to the Week 9 grades!With the NFL trade deadline coming up on Tuesday, we saw a lot of games this week that could end up having an impact on what happens over the next couple of days. For one, the Indianapolis Colts lost. The Colts have already been one of the busiest teams when it comes to trades, and there's been some speculation that they could trade Jonathan Taylor or Daniel Jones. After Sunday's loss to Dallas, the Colts are sitting at a very unimpressive 2-7, and it might make sense to just trade everyone. The Philadelphia Eagles also lost. Howie Roseman loves to make a deal, and with the Eagles now sitting at 2-7 after losing to the NFC East's top team, the Giants, he already worked one out on Monday. It could even make sense for the Jets to go into fire sale mode after dropping to 2-7 following a loss to the Chiefs.

        Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Reds were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year in their respective leagues on Monday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. McGonigle earned 28 of 30 first-place votes, beating out the Guardians' Parker Messick and the Red Sox's Payton Tolle. Stewart, meanwhile, beat the Mets' Carson Benge and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt.Because McGonigle and Stewart were both with the major-league team for long enough to earn a full year of service time, the Tigers and Reds will each receive a Prospect Promotion Incentive pick in the 2027 MLB Draft. The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    National League: Sal Stewart, RedsStewart won the battle of Old School stats vs. New School stats here. Though he only posted 2.0 WAR, he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The only names from that list to not win the award either faced another player from the list or played before Rookie of the Year was awarded. Everyone else has taken home the hardware, just as Stewart did Monday evening.
Overall, Stewart appeared in all 162 games, hitting .263/.330/.457 (117 OPS+) with 25 doubles, 32 homers, 112 RBI, 87 runs and 15 steals. Stewart earned 20 of the 30 available first-place votes.Player1st2nd3rd4th5thPointsSal Stewart, Reds205131170Carson Benge, Mets731242107JJ Wetherholt, Cardinals31265299Nolan McLean, Mets679770TJ Rumfield, Rockies3391049Logan Henderson, Brewers11310Bryce Eldridge, Brewers22Didier Fuentes, Braves22A.J. title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni denies giving his fans the middle finger after division loss: 'Absolutely not' - CBS Sports
description: Sirianni said the accusations were a 'surprise' to him, which come after Philadelphia's first home loss to the Gi
body:
Sirianni said the accusations were a 'surprise' to him, which come after Philadelphia's first home loss to the Giants in 13 years.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles season isn't exactly going as planned, with a losing record and major injuries. When struggles come in sports, frustrations typically follow and Philly's head coach has been accused of letting out those frustrations with a well-known gesture after their 19-11 divisional loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, the team's first loss in Philadelphia to the Giants since 2013.  Nick Sirianni was called out for what some believe was the head coach giving fans the middle finger as he walked off the field after the Week 9 defeat. In the video, Sirianni looks at his hand, then the middle finger is raised higher than the others as he approaches the tunnel.  Nick Sirianni was asked if he was flipping fans off while walking off the field yesterday.   "Absolutely not."   #Eagles  https://t.co/fqKylEJGxw— Cory Nidoh (@Cory_Nidoh) November 9, 2026Sirianni denies any ill will on whatever his hand was doing at the time, saying, "Absolutely not. That was a surprise to me. Absolutely not."This is not the first time Sirianni and Eagles fans have clashed. In 2024, Sirianni was booed by some fans at Lincoln Financial Field, with some yelling for him to be fired during a game against the then 1-5 Cleveland Browns. Fans weren't happy that the Eagles were struggling, coming off a bye, against an easy opponent. Philadelphia went went on to win the game, though narrowly at 20-16. As he was walking off the field, Sirianni cupped his ears and yelled at fans. At first, he said he was just "having fun" and was "excited to get the win," but then reversed his messaging, issuing an apology to Eagles fans.  
"What I was really doing, I was trying to bring energy yesterday, energy, enthusiasm, and I'm sorry and disappointed on how my energy was directed at the end of the game," he said at the time. "And, you know, my energy should be all in on coaching, motivating and celebrating with our guys. And so I've got to have better wisdom and discernment of when to use that energy and that wasn't the time." Another notable move from the head coach this Sunday was how long it took to start his press conference, with him taking the podium over an hour after the game ended. He said during that time he was talking to players and didn't reveal exactly what it was about. Typically, press conferences begin much sooner than that for a head coach, so many online pointed out the oddity. The Eagles currently sit at 2-7 and are on a seven-game losing streak. This marks the worst start during Sirianni's time with the team. This marks the first time since 1999 that the team has started 2-7.  
If Sirianni wasn't in the hot seat before (he was), he certainly is now after a bad divisional loss that put them in last in the NFC East.

title: Fantasy football Week 10 risers and fallers: Bryce Young surges, Stafford slips - CBS Sports
description: Bryce Young is climbing the Fantasy ranks after a breakout performance, while Matthew Stafford's struggles raise
body:
Bryce Young is climbing the Fantasy ranks after a breakout performance, while Matthew Stafford's struggles raise concerns

    5:48 pm ET

        Prominent players we projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 10 as of Monday evening: Josh Jacobs, Rhamondre Stevenson, Omar Cooper Jr., Xavier Worthy, Ladd McConkey, Jake FergusonAt the bottom of this article are my Week 10 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information. Risers Bryce Young, QB, Panthers
In some ways, Young was always going to be a Week 10 riser. That's because he faced the Broncos in Week 9 and will play against the Saints in Week 10. What we didn't expect was Young throwing for 276 yards and three touchdowns against one of the best pass defenses in the NFL. Young has now produced multiple touchdowns in five of eight starts and at least 276 yards passing in six of eight. Against the Saints, he looks close to a must-start option.
C.J. Stroud, QB, Texans
Stroud gets the Browns this week, which is not a good matchup for QBs at all. I'm not sure it matters. With Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, and Marvin Harrison, Stroud has arguably the deepest collection of pass catchers in the NFL. The Texans' inability to sustain a run game has led to Stroud throwing 35 times per game, and he's averaging a very impressive eight yards per attempt. I am not sure I see a matchup left in the Fantasy regular season that will cause me to rank Stroud outside of the top 12.Breece Hall, RB, Jets
In his first game back, Hall had 18 touches. That's enough to move him back inside my top 20 running backs, especially with four teams on a bye and more injuries to the position in Week 9. I actually think against the Bills you may be able to start both Hall and Braelon Allen as RB2s. They face the Bills in Week 10 and heading into Monday night, the Bills have given up the second-most points to opposing running backs.Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers, Ravens
I am not sure Jacoby Brissett can save the Ravens season, but I do expect him to save the Fantasy season for Henry and Flowers. Brissett has been mostly bad so far this season, but still levels above Joe Fagnano. Teams will have to respect the pass at least a little bit, which should open up running lanes for Henry. Flowers has already proven that he can deliver with Tyler Huntley, and projects as a borderline top 12 wide receiver once again. What will be interesting is the Ravens run/pass split. Brissett has led a pass-heavy offense in Arizona the past two years. I would expect a balanced approach from Baltimore, especially against the Chargers.
Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints
I'm not ready to rank Tyson as a starter yet, but I can see the light at the end of the tunnel. He was second on the team in targets in his debut despite running just 34.8% of the team's routes. I expect him to be over 50% this week and inch towards 75% in the coming month. This week he may not need more than 50% in a shootout against the Panthers. View Tyson as a low-end WR3, but he has more reason for optimism than most of the guys projected in that range.FallersMatthew Stafford, QB, Rams
If Puka Nacua's knee injury is serious, Stafford may fall out of the top 24, but even with Nacua, Stafford is a faller. He already has his most interceptions in a season since 2023 and he hasn't reached even 230 yards since Week 5. His 6.9 yards per pass attempt this year is tied for his worst mark since joining the Rams. Stafford could still turn this around, but we need to see it before we want to start him again. Hopefully Terrance Ferguson will help whenever he gets back.Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns
If we can't trust Judkins against the Saints, I don't know who we can trust him against. He even got an extra 10 minutes in Week 9 thanks to overtime and still only scored 5.5 PPR Fantasy points. The two major problems are horrible rush efficiency and Dylan Sampson hogging the running back targets. We have no reason to expect either to change in Week 10 when the Browns take on the Texans.
Devin Singletary, RB, Giants
This is actually good news: Cam Skattebo is expected back! Singletary should go back to a role on third downs and the two-minute drill, which makes him a desperation flex at best. Skattebo is ranked about where Singletary was last week, around RB24. This is a huge opportunity for the second-year back even if the Commanders run defense has been good for most of the season.Nico Collins, WR, Texans
It is rare that we have a quarterback as a riser and his number one receiver as a faller. The problem is that Collins, despite an amazing touchdown catch on Sunday, barely looks like a WR1. Collins hasn't seen more than five targets in a game since Week 5. In his last three games, he has a 14.4% snap share and he's only played 62.9% of the offensive snaps. The Texans have a heavy rotation at receiver right now and it is capping Collins' upside. You're still probably starting him as a WR2 but he is no longer a must-start in leagues where you only start two receivers.Brenton Strange, TE, Jaguars
This has less to do with Strange than it does the Jaguars blowing everyone out. Trevor Lawrence has thrown a combined 40 passes in his last two games. Strange's best games came when the volume was much higher. This week they are 10-point favorites against the Titans. There is no reason to hope for more than 25 pass attempts from Lawrence. Strange is still a high-end TE2 but he will probably need a touchdown to score double-digit Fantasy points.

title: Winners and losers from the first week of women's hoops: JuJu Watkins returns, two players get turned around - CBS Sports
description: College basketball is back, and we're recapping the good, the bad and the weird of the first week
body:
College basketball is back, and we're recapping the good, the bad and the weird of the first week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026-27 women's college basketball season is already off to a rousing start, and spoiler alert: South Carolina is still very good! The Gamecocks got off to a 2-0 start, with both wins coming over ranked teams, and Dawn Staley's squad firmly looks like the team to beat this season.
        
            
                Women's college basketball rankings: Michigan up to No. 2 in AP Top 25 after UConn upset
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But below them in the rankings, there were storylines galore. It was a week filled with records, including the debut of the tallest player in women's college basketball history, Texas Tech's 7-foot-1 Stephanie Okechukwu, and the most lopsided game in women's Division I history, LSU's 109-point blowout of Texas Southern. It also included a vanishing event, a historic upset, an iconic return, a couple of headline-generating gaffes and even a dazzling debut from a WNBA draftee.Without further ado, here are winners and losers from the opening week of action:Winner: The Michigan WolverinesThere's no reason to get cute off the top. On Thursday night at the Crisler Center, the Wolverines got one of the biggest wins in program history, defeating then-No. 2 UConn, 77-66. Coming into the game, the Huskies had won 39 regular-season games in a row, dating back to Feb. 6, 2025.
The win took Michigan from No. 5 to No. 2 in the AP poll, and sent a message that the Wolverines are a true Final Four contender. It was a marquee moment for head coach Kim Barnes Arico and her star-studded junior class, most of whom came into the program together as freshmen to do something special."That's why we came here. We had belief in coach. We had belief in the program, and we wanted to help build it, to take it places it hasn't been," guard Olivia Olson said. "I'm just proud to be part of it."Te'Yala Delfosse, one of the more unheralded members of that class, led the way with 22 points, nine rebounds and four 3-pointers. Olson added 10 points and eight rebounds, while Syla Swords had 10 points and five boards.
Loser: Sense of directionThere are always some kinks to work out early in the season, but last week that notion was taken to new heights not once, but twice. Two players in two separate games in Division I women's basketball on Friday shot the ball into the wrong basket. Yes, we had two basketball own goals. 
The first came from Karma Wynn of Northwestern State, who got mixed up during a full-court press after her team inbounded the ball in the first quarter and scored two points for Arkansas. Arkansas ended up winning the game 89-59, so Wynn's basket didn't decide the game by any means.However, later that day, an own goal almost did impact the final result when Emma Christiano of New Mexico State also got turned around after intercepting an inbound play. That came at a crucial time in the game, though, with Southern Utah up 61-60 with 20.9 seconds remaining. Christiano thought she had put her team ahead, but instead she extended Southern Utah's lead to 63-60.
Christiano's teammates had her back, though; New Mexico State scored four points in the final 20 seconds to win the game 64-63. We all do inexplicable things sometimes, and hopefully both Wynn and Christiano can laugh at their mistakes. And hey, at the very least, since they shared the gaffe, they can take the heat off of one another.Winner: JuJu Watkins' returnAfter 588 days on the sidelines, JuJu Watkins officially returned to the women's college basketball world last week and immediately showed the world what it has been missing.In her first game, which No. 3 USC won 100-68 over UNLV, Watkins had 21 points, five rebounds, two steals and a block in 25 minutes. The only blip on that day was her shooting, as she was 0 of 5 from outside. However, she immediately got back on track in the second game, with a staggering 32 points, 16 rebounds, six assists, five steals and one block in a 118-40 victory over Utah State. In that game, Watkins was 10 of 19 from the field for 52.6% and 4 of 7 from 3-point land for 57.1%.
It will be interesting to see how Watkins holds up against tougher competition, and we won't have to wait long; on Sunday, Nov. 15 USC travels to Greenville to face No. 1 South Carolina. Go ahead and clear your schedules.
        
            
                JuJu Watkins returns after 588 days: USC star on family, the ACL tear and why 'there is no if' for the Trojans
                
                    Erica Ayala                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Loser: The Foundry ClassicBecause of Michigan's big win over UConn, Duke fell from No. 4 to No. 5 in the rankings this week despite getting off to a 2-0 start with fairly comfortable wins over Green Bay and Florida Atlantic. However, the box scores don't accurately describe how bizarre the first week of the regular season was for Kara Lawson and her team.Originally -- and up until last Thursday -- Duke was scheduled to play their second game of the season against North Texas at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. The game was to be a homecoming for Duke junior Arianna Robinson and freshman Bella Flemings, who grew up in the area. The game was part of The Foundry Classic, which was billed as a two-day event that would see players from each team "participate through dedicated residency spaces for each program, providing opportunities for students to engage with college athletes beyond the basketball court."
Among other things, Lawson and North Texas head coach Jason Burton were supposed to be part of a panel on Saturday evening, the night before the game.But on Thursday evening, USA Today reported that Duke was reaching out to teams in other conferences in "urgent need of a replacement game" for the weekend. And on Friday, both Duke and North Texas announced that the game had been canceled "due to circumstances beyond the control of participating institutions." It is currently unknown what exactly transpired, but it seems The Foundry Classic never materialized.Duke was able to schedule a last-minute road game at Florida Atlantic on Sunday, which it won, 78-56. 
Winner: Addi Mack's second half against South CarolinaAs exciting as the first week of the season was, there aren't many individual performances that I'm still going to be thinking about come March. The exception to that rule might be Addi Mack's second half against South Carolina in the season opener in Paris.Maryland was down 28 points at the half and 31 points in the third quarter, but with 46 seconds left in the game, the Gamecocks were holding onto a six-point lead by their claws. South Carolina ended up holding onto a 101-93 victory, but the Terrapins were so impressive in a loss that they went up one place in the rankings to No. 19.And it was Mack who powered the valiant comeback attempt, with 31 points in the second half, even bettering Gabby Williams' second-half performance in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals -- by points, at least. For the game, Mack was 14 of 20 from the field and 6 of 10 from outside for 35 points, six assists, three rebounds and two steals. Even though the performance came in a loss, it deserves to be a winner.
Loser: The 2026 Chicago SkyYes, I know that this is a women's college basketball piece, and that the Chicago Sky got dunked on plenty during the WNBA season after the team traded Angel Reese and saw her immediately take the Atlanta Dream to the Finals. But they're in the spotlight again because of the performance of Ajša Sivka, a Slovenian player whom the Sky actually drafted No. 10 overall in the 2025 WNBA draft.Sivka didn't join the team in 2025, and this spring she opted to sign with the Kentucky Wildcats in lieu of joining the Sky for the 2026 season. And she is acclimating just fine to the college game -- on Sunday against N.C. State, Sivka had 32 points, five rebounds and three assists in Kentucky's 93-78 win. Her efficiency was more impressive than her stat line -- she was 11 of 17 from the field and a staggering 8 of 12 from outside.In press, she said that she chose to come to Kentucky because of the development she could get under head coach Kenny Brooks, noting that the individual work this summer has already helped her improve. 
"I just wanted to be ready and feel confident once I go there," she said, referring to the WNBA. Brooks said she is "definitely one of the best players in the country."The Sky do retain her WNBA rights, so they might be winners in the long run. But they certainly could have used a shooter like her in the 2026 season.

title: Gotham FC move NWSL semi to Icahn Stadium over pitch quality concerns - CBS Sports
description: Gotham were originally set to play Sunday's semifinal at Sports Illustrated Stadium, where the pitch was describe
body:
Gotham were originally set to play Sunday's semifinal at Sports Illustrated Stadium, where the pitch was described as 'atrocious' following their quarterfinal match against the Seattle Reign
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Gotham FC will play Sunday's NWSL semifinal against the Kansas City Current at Icahn Stadium over concerns about the quality of the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, which was described as "atrocious" during the team's quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign.The NWSL Shield winners announced the venue shift on Monday, less than a week before the semifinal. Icahn Stadium is a smaller venue on Manhattan's Randall's Island that seats 5,000 and has been sparingly used by Gotham, who have played the vast majority of their home games at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, N.J. since 2021. Sports Illustrated Stadium seats 25,000 and welcomed nearly 13,000 for Sunday's 1-0 win over the Reign.The quarterfinal match, though, was marred by complaints about the playing surface from both teams. Reign head coach Laura Harvey described the field as "shit" in a post-match interview with ESPN, while captain Jess Fishlock called it "atrocious." Gotham head coach Juan Carlos Amoros also apologized for the quality of the surface after the NWSL fined the club $10,000 in the build-up to the quarterfinal match."We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," captain Tierna Davidson said in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league, or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision. You have turned every ground where we have played into home, and that does not change on Sunday. We have never needed a perfect setting to make a place ours. Bring everything you have on Sunday, and we will leave it all on the field."
The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium appeared to show the wear and tear from recent events, not least of which was Gotham's regular season slate. Gotham are the secondary tenants at the venue, which is owned by New Jersey's Hudson County but counts MLS' Red Bull New York as the primary tenants and operators of the facility. The stadium was also the site of a rugby doubleheader the weekend before Gotham's quarterfinal against the Reign, which led Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell to describe the surface as "sandy" and "unstable."The Red Bulls will still play a friendly on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium against Club America. The friendly will take place during the men's international break, so several first-team players will miss the match, which will serve as the final game of their season since they missed out on the MLS Cup playoffs for a second season in a row."We wish Gotham FC the best of luck in their semifinal at Icahn Stadium," Red Bull New York told CBS Sports in a statement. "We look forward to our match on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium."
Not Gotham's first trip to IcahnGotham have staged two games at Icahn Stadium in the last year and change – a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage match in 2025 and their 3-2 win over the Reign in July. There is the perception of convenience for the club's fans based in the city of New York, who would otherwise have to trek to New Jersey to attend a game. As far as public transportation goes, though, Icahn Stadium is only accessible via the M35 bus; a footbridge connecting Randall's Island to 125th Street is also an option, as is driving to the stadium."It's nice for folks who live in New York to have a somewhat closer venue," Jen Muller, a longtime member of the official Gotham supporters group Cloud 9, told CBS Sports last year. "I know it's not ideal for a lot of them, too, because there's one bus that comes here, but you adapt."The pitch at Icahn Stadium, which has also hosted New York City FC II matches this year, is not expected to be an issue and was not during the Concacaf match in 2025.
"I don't really want to talk too much about it, but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros said at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that, so this pitch here is outstanding."Logistics plague NWSL playoffsGotham's move to Icahn comes despite the fact that they avoided a scheduling conflict with Sunday's results. The NWSL's broadcast slots for this year's semifinals were Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC; the Washington Spirit will host the Utah Royals on Saturday, while Gotham will take on the Current on Sunday.For Gotham, the Sunday time slot was the preferred option because of a pre-existing scheduling conflict with the Red Bulls' Saturday friendly against Club America. They had to wait out the result of the Spirit's quarterfinal with the Portland Thorns, though, since the Thorns would have been unable to host a semifinal at 9 a.m. local time. Gotham seemed destined to return to Sports Illustrated Stadium once they avoided the scheduling conflict but the quality of the pitch caused new concerns.
The Spirit, meanwhile, avoided a scheduling conflict of their own. They were originally set to host the Royals at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders, because their usual venue of Audi Field was instead hosting Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy. The college football game has since been pushed to a later slot that day, Spirit CEO Kim Stone crediting Audi Field owners D.C. United and sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union for underwriting "the additional costs necessary to bring this semifinal match home."The issues stem from the fact that many NWSL teams are secondary tenants in their home stadiums, the Spirit included – MLS' D.C. United own and operate Audi Field. Some, like the Royals and the Orlando Pride, benefit from sharing ownership groups with MLS clubs, while the Current own and operate CPKC Stadium. The rest often rent the local MLS team's stadium, Gotham and the Spirit included, but it creates other unique conflicts for teams with more control over their venues. The Current's quarterfinal against Angel City on Saturday, for example, kicked off at 11 a.m. local time in order to fit the broadcast slot on CBS.

body:
Puka Nacua's injury leaves a massive Fantasy void, but these trade targets and waiver-wire options could help save your season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As soon as Myles Garrett came back and made a huge impact for the Rams on defense, the Rams offense lost one of its impact players when head coach Sean McVay announced Puka Nacua will "be out a good amount of time" with an MCL/PCL sprain and turf toe.For the Rams, and for Fantasy Football managers, there is no replacing Nacua. He's averaged 13.3 targets, 10 catches, 102.1 receiving yards and 24.8 PPR points per game. The man is a unicorn.  Trying to guess the Rams' next move is dangerous. When Nacua went down with an injury in Week 1 of the 2024 season, everyone assumed Tutu Atwell, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Whittington would all take on more work. They did, but none averaged more than the 11.4 PPR points Atwell reeled in over five games (he also averaged 6.8 targets per game). That includes tight end Colby Parkinson, by the way.  Moreover, in those games, the Rams went 2-3, averaged 18.8 points per game and ran the ball 44% of their plays.  
Their offense simply was not the same without Nacua. And it won't be the same this time around, either. Not until Davante Adams comes back, but that figures to be by Week 12 at the earliest. And tight end Terrance Ferguson will be "another couple of weeks" out, according to McVay, who said before Week 9 that he hurt his hamstring in practice.What should Fantasy managers do?Don't look to the Rams depth chart to find a winning solution at receiver. Look to other receivers around the league. Remember, the goal here is to simply find a receiver who you can start with some confidence -- a guy who can average six targets per week, preferably with a good quarterback on a team that throws a lot, would be a good enough Band-Aid. Receivers to trade forCarnell Tate, Titans: He should be healthy coming out of the bye, and he's seen at least six targets in four of his past five. His schedule is mostly good; Cam Ward has made some slow progress in his game, and the Titans probably won't have many low-pass-volume game scripts. He also shouldn't cost too much in trade. Tate is the receiver on this list I'd chase the most.  
Jalen Coker, Panthers: Coker has been on a dry spell, much like the Panthers, but he obviously plays a lot and works as a short-area outlet for Bryce Young. His target volume has sunk in his past three games and the Panthers offensively are finding ways to stay competitive despite a depleted offensive line. His schedule is mostly great — until Weeks 15 through 17. Maybe the most appealing part of acquiring Coker is the very low cost it'll take to get him given his recent weak stats.  Jordyn Tyson, Saints: The rookie had a sensational 31.3% target-per-route run rate in his debut last week, lining up in the slot just as much as he did out wide. He definitely flashed quicks out of his breaks and the same kind of acceleration we saw in college. The Saints haven't found a reliable run game all year, and because their remaining schedule isn't too daunting, we should see them throw a lot. That should mean Tyson winds up second on the team in targets from this point forward.  Denzel Boston, Browns: Cleveland's best threat outside the numbers, Boston has gotten at least seven targets in five of his past six, and he has nine red-zone targets on the year. Unfortunately, Boston's been above 10 PPR points in just three of those six. He does see an 83.6% catchable target rate, the fourth-lowest compared to 22 other players with at least 60 targets, so his quarterback play does keep his ceiling low. But the Browns' run game is a mess and their schedule after the Week 11 bye is amazing.   
KC Concepcion, Browns: Like Boston, Concepcion gets a lot of targets, but unlike Boston, they're all mostly short-area screens and slants. That leads to easier completions (his catchable target rate is slightly better at 85.5%), but his floor is lower. Then again, if the Browns schedule is good for the pass game after Week 11, then Concepcion should be able to break a bunch of big plays after the catch. That'll be his only pathway to huge numbers, since he has a grand total of two red-zone targets in 2026.  If you can get them cheap ... Nico Collins and Garrett Wilson are also good receivers to target, but the people who roster them might be a little delusional in what they'd want in return. If you're willing to pay a pretty penny, then go after one of those two before the cheaper thrills listed above.  Receivers to add off waiversTank Dell, Texans (22% rostered): The dude had nine targets despite a 55% route rate in a blowout win over the Chargers. Seven of the nine targets were deep shots, of which he caught two. There's no doubt that C.J. Stroud loves having him back on the field, and the Texans' run game has been a wreck all year. Therefore, the Texans' chase for a playoff spot will go through Stroud's arm.  
Makai Lemon, Eagles (59% rostered): You'll have to deal with his Week 10 bye, but the Eagles are heading toward a lost season with a depleted defense, making it more likely that the offense will throw a lot. Even with DeVonta Smith coming back at some point, Lemon should still be in the six-target range.  Caleb Douglas, Dolphins (73% rostered on CBS; lower on other platforms): It's beginning to look like Douglas will work as Miami's No. 1 receiver moving forward. He's got very good size and good speed to go with it, and the Dolphins offense will probably lean pass-heavy. Maybe four tough matchups are in front of him, but he should be another youngster worth your time.  Adonai Mitchell, Jets (63% rostered): His seven-target, zero-catch outing against the Chiefs might deter you, but Geno Smith has been completely willing to keep firing at Mitchell. And let's be fair, a week ago he had 142 yards and a touchdown. His schedule gets prickly once you get near the Fantasy playoffs.  
Tutu Atwell, Rams (1% rostered): When the Rams were without Nacua for five games in 2024, Atwell stepped in and was the only pass-catcher to notch more than two weeks with double-digit PPR points. I'd be surprised if Atwell was just as good this time around, but he's a known quantity to this coaching staff -- they signed him to a crazy one-year deal last year, barely used him, then let him go in free agency to the Dolphins before trading for him before the season started!   If you don't mind streaming ... Ryan Flournoy (59% rostered), Demario Douglas (82% rostered on CBS; lower on other platforms), Jordan Watkins (25% rostered), Mack Hollins (12% rostered) and Xavier Hutchinson (6% rostered) are all worth taking a peek at. Hutchinson, like Dell, should play a lot in the slot for the Texans' pass-heavy offense.

title: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew feared to have suffered a torn UCL, could be out for season, per report - CBS Sports
description: Carson Beck would get the start if Minshew is sidelined
body:
Carson Beck would get the start if Minshew is sidelined
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals offensive injuries continue to pile up. Shortly after head coach Mike LaFleur announced wide receiver Michael Wilson would be ruled out for the year with a neck injury and added there was a chance Gardner Minshew misses Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams, reports came out that the quarterback is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.According to NFL Network, Minshew could be out for the season and face "months of rehab," pending further testing. Minshew reportedly suffered the injury before halftime but played through it in last week's 17-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks. If Minshew is sidelined, Carson Beck would be the next man up. Beck would be the third quarterback to start for the Cardinals this season. Jacoby Brissett began the year as their starter before being benched and traded to the Baltimore Ravens earlier this month. Since Beck would be the team's only QB on the depth chart if Minshew is out for the year, team reportedly acted fast to get some backup. On Monday, the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad, according to ESPN. This marks Johnson's 15th NFL team in 14 seasons.Beck was drafted in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 65 overall. The two-time College Football Playoff national champion has yet to make an appearance in the NFL. He would be the third rookie quarterback to start a game this season, joining Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels and Washington Commanders seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis. 
The 24-year-old spent five years at Georgia and his last collegiate season with Miami (FL). He finished with 338 completions, a conference high, for 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. His 72.4 completion percentage was also a conference high.In 55 total college games, he had 966 completions for 11,725 yards, 88 touchdowns and 32 interceptions. After Brissett's eight games, the team made a change at QB during the third quarter of their Nov. 1 game against the Cowboys, putting in Minshew. Beck was promoted to backup quarterback, with Brissett demoted to the third-string QB shortly before his exit from Arizona.Minshew played two games, with a 71.7 completion percentage, 354 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, going 0-1 in starts.
The Cardinals currently sit at 3-6 and are in fourth place in the NFC West.

title: Jordan Davis trade grades: Eagles kickstart rebuild, Jaguars push for 2026 AFC and Super Bowl titles - CBS Sports
description: Grading how both squads made out in the biggest trade on the eve of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline
body:
Grading how both squads made out in the biggest trade on the eve of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Jacksonville Jaguars capped their flurry of activity on the eve of the NFL's 2026 trade deadline with a blockbuster: they traded a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Davis was the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia and was also a starter on the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX title team in the 2024 season. Jacksonville doesn't have to worry about a long-term contract with Davis since Philadelphia extended Davis on a three-year, $78 million extension this past offseason. On Monday, the Jaguars have relinquished a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Davis, Atlanta Falcons Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.   Meanwhile, the Eagles now have 10 draft picks in the first two rounds of the NFL Draft across the next three years. They have their own first-round pick and second-round pick, plus the Jaguars' first-round pick in 2027. They have their own first-round pick and own second-round pick plus the New England Patriots' first-round pick (A.J. Brown trade) and the Baltimore Ravens' second-round pick (Cam Jurgens trade) in 2028. In 2029, they have their own first-round pick, their own second-round pick and the Jaguars' second-round pick (Jordan Davis trade).So how does each side grade out in Monday evening's blockbuster deal? Let's dive in.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jacksonville Jaguars: B-The Jaguars are right to go all in for the 2026 season. The Buffalo Bills (6-1) have one of the leakiest secondaries in the NFL, allowing 254.7 passing yards per game (the third-most in the entire NFL). The Denver Broncos (7-2) have offensive inconsistency issues because of quarterback Bo Nix, whose 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is the second-worst among 31 qualified quarterbacks this season. Nix's 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is mere decimal points ahead of Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 5.6 air yards per pass attempt to avoid being dead last in the league. Mahomes' league-worst air yards per pass attempt figure has more to do with the Chiefs' limited passing game options than an unwillingness to throw the ball downfield like Nix.The AFC North-leading Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, and he will be 43 years old by the time the playoffs begin. Jacksonville beat the Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) in a narrow, one-score game earlier this season, and the New England Patriots (5-4) just got decimated at home (45-27) by quarterback Jordan Love and his Green Bay Packers.Jacksonville's timing is right, but the price they paid for Davis is not. A first-round pick and a second-round pick for Davis isn't all that different from what the Chicago Bears gave up (2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth-round pick) for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, the best defensive tackle in football at the moment. Sure, the Jaguars were never going to get Simmons since he was on an AFC South division rival, the Tennessee Titans, but couldn't they have gotten Davis for a slightly cheaper price? The Bears are getting a player whose 17 sacks over the last two seasons are the most in the league among defensive tackles, while Davis has just 9.5 career sacks.
Yes, Davis can be incredibly impactful in the run game just because of his frame (6-feet-6-inches tall while weighing 336 pounds), but one would think that the Jaguars would have been able to acquire a more well-rounded defensive tackle at the price point of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Davis will certainly help Jacksonville, but what they gave up for him was a little rich. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia Eagles: AHats off to Eagles general manager Howie Roseman because he's done it again. He recognized that the 2026 season was dead with quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) sidelined, and the team was on a seven-game losing streak, putting their record at 2-7 through nine games. Roseman also extended two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jalen Carter on a four-year, $152 million extension last offseason, and it was clear that Philadelphia likely wouldn't be able to keep both Carter and Davis for years to come in order to have a well-balanced roster. Roseman was able to trade away the lesser player of the two, and he recouped first-round and second-round draft capital in the deal. He couldn't have asked for anything more, and he'll be able to rebuild the Eagles in no time with 10 picks in the first two rounds of the draft across the next three years.

        There is always something brewing when Kansas and Kentucky face off, especially considering that Tyran Stokes picked Kansas over Kentucky to end a feverish recruiting battle in April. The potential future No. 1 pick will lace 'em up against a coach in Mark Pope, who spent months trying to woo Stokes to Lexington and drew heat from every corner of BBN when he came up short. It's the story of this game, but Tuesday's Champions Classic is also a golden opportunity for both No. 15 Kansas and No. 24 Kentucky to show that they're far better than their current national status.Let's dive into the nuts and bolts of this blue-blood matchup, starting with projected starting lineups:Kentucky: G Zoom Diallo, G Alex Wilkins, F Milan Momcilovic, F Ousmane N'Diaye, C Malachi Moreno
Kansas: G Taylen Kinney, G Tre White, G Tyran Stokes, F Trey Kaufman-Renn, F Keanu Dawes
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kentucky vs. Kansas: Need to knowAll eyes on Mr. Stokes: Recruiting drama aside, Stokes is also a real matchup problem for Kentucky in this spot. Pope does not have many good options to handle Kansas' 6-8 freshman wing, who is too big for guards and way too fast for most forwards. Sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic is in Lexington to bang 3-pointers, but Kentucky needs him to play the best defensive game of the season. Momcilovic on Stokes is a matchup Kentucky may have to live with, and it's going to be something Kansas coach Bill Self targets from the jump. If Momcilovic can't handle Stokes' bully-ball drives, Kentucky may have to try Zoom Diallo. Maybe redshirt-freshman wing Braydon Hawthorne could also be part of the solution. Hawthorne's got an enormous wingspan and has impressed defensively so far. Stokes is a problem for everybody, but especially this Kentucky roster. If Stokes goes off, Kentucky is in hot water.Mark Pope's big game woes: Kentucky is 29-26 against high-major teams under Pope. That is far from the standard. One common denominator has been a halfcourt offense gone awry. Self is going to do whatever it takes to keep Kentucky from getting free for its patented transition 3-pointers. If you can make this Kentucky team execute in the halfcourt, there are many more outs for Kansas' defense. But that's easier said than done. Kansas' starting lineup has barely played together this season after Kaufman-Renn's late addition to the roster. Kentucky has plenty of shooting and length surrounding a big man in Malachi Moreno who can really pass the basketball. If Kansas' defense is not connected, Kentucky has the offensive personnel to make it pay. 
Melvin Council Jr. broke his foot; what does it mean? Kansas is losing its dawg and its soul. Council is the high-energy sparkplug who is a voracious defender, an all-out competitor and one of the fastest guards in all of college basketball. Kansas will absolutely miss his speed. Self has a decision to make, whether to go big with Keanu Dawes or Christian Reeves to guard Moreno or to stay small and insert Toledo transfer Leroy Blyden Jr., who is quite fast and owns a feathery jumper. That optionality is a good thing. I also think it does just ramp up the usage rate for Stokes and Kaufman-Renn. I'd love to see Stokes and TKR get rolling in the pick-and-roll game together. Those are two giant playmakers who could put Kentucky's defense into some rough positions. They've just barely played together this year, so it's hard to imagine the Stokes-TKR, two-man game humming on all cylinders right away.Where to watch Kentucky vs. Kansas liveDate: Tuesday, Nov. 10 | Time: 9:30 p.m. ETLocation: United Center -- ChicagoTV: ESPN | Live stream: fubo (Try for free)Kentucky vs. Kansas predictionKansas' full team had only been practicing together for only three (!) weeks. Then starting guard Melvin Council Jr. broke his foot Monday, forcing Bill Self to recalibrate again. Kansas has the more talented roster on paper, but I wouldn't be surprised if there are still some kinks to be ironed out that were not exposed in romps over solid mid-majors like Fordham and Middle Tennessee. Is Kentucky good enough to press those hot spots? Maybe. Kentucky's 3-point shooting is the path to popping the upset. Kansas does not profile as a high-volume 3-point shooting team with Trey Kaufman-Renn, Tre White, Tyran Stokes and Keanu Dawes on the floor together. On the other hand, Milan Momcilovic is the best shooter in the sport. If Kentucky can rebound and run, it is very capable of drilling double-digit treys. That's rarely going to be in the range of potential outcomes for Kansas, who will rely heavily on paint points and free throws to score efficiently.
The Council injury likely means Self will go big, sacrificing some of the pace for even more rebounding. A front line of Dawes, Stokes and Kaufman-Renn might not make many 3s, but it creates some awkward matchups for Kentucky. Can Momcilovic defend Stokes without fouling a freshman who is a foul-drawing machine? Does Kentucky ditch that idea altogether and put a bulldog veteran guard like Zoom Diallo onto Stokes, stay home on everyone else and try to bait Stokes into taking a million shots over a smaller defender? Making Stokes one-dimensional is better than allowing him to shred as a scorer and creator. Kansas' offensive rebounding feels inevitable, but Kentucky's shooting and length make it very live. Its up-and-down guards just need to play clean in this one, or UK is dead on arrival. The pick: Kentucky +5.5
